steps.tx: **Breast cancer** is the commonest non-skin cancer in women. The main drivers are **female sex**, rising **age** and long **estrogen exposure**: about 70% of cases are found at 55 or older. A first-degree relative with the disease doubles the risk, yet only 20% of patients have any family history. Inherited **BRCA1** and **BRCA2** mutations explain a small share of cases.
steps.say: Breast cancer is the commonest non-skin cancer in women. The main drivers are female sex, rising age and long exposure to estrogen. About 70 percent of cases are found at 55 or older. A first-degree relative with breast cancer doubles the risk, but only 20 percent of patients have any family history at all. Inherited BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations explain a small share of cases.

rows: Risk climbs with age; median age at diagnosis 63
Risk up about four- to fivefold

steps.tx: A suspicious lump goes through **triple assessment**: clinical examination, breast imaging and tissue diagnosis. Imaging is **mammography**, with ultrasound and sometimes MRI, and both breasts are imaged because up to 3% have hidden disease on the other side. The diagnosis rests on an **image-guided core biopsy**, which also gives the grade and the receptor status. A normal mammogram never clears a palpable lump.
steps.say: A suspicious lump goes through triple assessment: clinical examination, breast imaging, and tissue diagnosis. Imaging means mammography, with ultrasound and sometimes MRI. Both breasts are imaged, because up to 3 percent of women have hidden disease on the other side. The diagnosis rests on an image-guided core biopsy, which also gives the grade and the receptor status. Remember: a normal mammogram never clears a lump you can feel.

nodes.label: Imaging
nodes.sub: Mammography of both breasts, ultrasound, MRI if needed

steps.tx: Most invasive cancers are **ductal**. About 10-15% are **lobular**: usually ER positive and HER2 negative, and recognised by loss of **E-cadherin**. Lobular cancer likes unusual sites such as the pleura, peritoneum, meninges, ovaries and gut, so a recurrence can present atypically. **DCIS** is malignancy still confined within the basement membrane: non-invasive, but treated.
steps.say: Most invasive breast cancers are ductal. About 10 to 15 percent are lobular. Lobular cancers are usually ER positive and HER2 negative, and they are recognised by loss of E-cadherin. They like unusual sites such as the pleura, peritoneum, meninges, ovaries and gut, so a recurrence can look atypical. Ductal carcinoma in situ, or DCIS, is malignancy still confined within the basement membrane. It is non-invasive, but it is treated.

points: Usual metastatic sites: soft tissue, lung, bone, liver, brain

right.title: Invasive lobular
points: Serosa, ovaries and gut: atypical recurrence

steps.tx: Receptor testing sorts invasive cancers into four **molecular subtypes**. **Luminal A** and **luminal B** are both ER positive; luminal B has lower PR or higher Ki67 and does worse. **HER2-enriched** tumours over-express HER2 and benefit from HER2-targeted drugs. **Triple-negative** cancer lacks ER, PR and HER2, and carries a poorer prognosis.
steps.say: Receptor testing sorts invasive breast cancers into four molecular subtypes. Luminal A and luminal B are both ER positive. Luminal B has lower PR or a higher Ki67, and a worse outcome. HER2-enriched tumours over-express HER2, and they benefit from HER2-targeted drugs. Triple-negative cancer lacks ER, PR and HER2, and it carries a poorer prognosis.

rows: ER positive, lower PR or higher Ki67
Endocrine therapy; chemotherapy if high risk

steps.tx: Staging uses **TNM**. The T category rises with size: over 2 cm is T2 and over 5 cm is T3, while spread to the **chest wall or skin** is T4, and **inflammatory cancer** is T4d. Stages I and II are early disease, stage III is **locally advanced** and stage IV is metastatic. Survival follows stage: over 99% at 5 years for stage I, about 29% for stage IV.
steps.say: Staging uses the TNM system. The T category rises with size. Over 2 centimetres is T2, and over 5 centimetres is T3. Spread to the chest wall or the skin is T4, and inflammatory cancer is T4d. Stages one and two are early disease, stage three is locally advanced, and stage four is metastatic. Survival follows stage: over 99 percent at 5 years for stage one, and about 29 percent for stage four.

steps.tx: Local control is **breast-conserving surgery** with whole-breast radiotherapy, or **mastectomy**. The axilla is staged at the same operation: **sentinel lymph node biopsy** when the nodes are clinically negative, **axillary clearance** when nodes are proven involved. After mastectomy, four or more positive nodes make chest wall and nodal radiotherapy mandatory; a node-negative tumour of 5 cm or less with clear margins needs none.
steps.say: Local control means breast-conserving surgery with whole-breast radiotherapy, or a mastectomy. The axilla is staged at the same operation. When the nodes are clinically negative, a sentinel lymph node biopsy is done. When nodes are proven to be involved, the axilla is cleared. After mastectomy, four or more positive nodes make radiotherapy to the chest wall and nodes mandatory. A node-negative tumour of 5 centimetres or less, with clear margins, needs none.

steps.tx: Systemic therapy follows the receptors. **ER-positive** disease gets endocrine therapy: **tamoxifen** or an **aromatase inhibitor**, adding ovarian suppression for selected premenopausal women. **HER2-positive** disease gets **trastuzumab**, often with pertuzumab, combined with chemotherapy, and the LVEF is monitored. **Triple-negative** disease relies on chemotherapy, with immunotherapy added. Bone metastases get a bisphosphonate.
steps.say: Systemic therapy follows the receptors. ER-positive disease gets endocrine therapy: tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor, with ovarian suppression added for selected premenopausal women. HER2-positive disease gets trastuzumab, often with pertuzumab, combined with chemotherapy, and the heart's ejection fraction is monitored. Triple-negative disease relies on chemotherapy, with immunotherapy added. Bone metastases are treated with a bisphosphonate.

steps.tx: Two presentations are easily mistaken for benign disease. **Paget disease of the nipple** looks like eczema of the nipple and areola but sits over DCIS or an invasive cancer. **Inflammatory breast cancer** causes rapid redness, swelling and **peau d'orange**; it is staged T4d. A 'mastitis' that does not settle on antibiotics needs a breast or skin biopsy.
